title: Generalized fluctuation-dissipation theorem and Einstein relation in rotating equilibrium
abstract: We derive a generalized fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT) for vector fields in rotating thermal equilibrium from an exact phase-space Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) relation. The resulting FDT contains rotation-induced tensorial contributions beyond a scalar thermal factor. In the local transport limit, we obtain a model-independent generalized Einstein relation with rotation in which, through second order in thermal vorticity, symmetric momentum diffusion depends on low-frequency spectral information beyond that encoded in the rotation-dependent dissipative drag. Remarkably, we find a new Einstein-type relation linking zero modes in the spectral function to the nonrotating drag coefficient. These zero modes underlie a new mechanism for the orbital polarization of heavy quarkonium. The same FDT constraint yields a modified detailed-balance relation whose first-order vortical correction is governed by transition polarization, without explicit dependence on the bath model. Our findings establish microscopic equilibrium constraints for studying rotating quantum matter in various fields.
summary: This theoretical work generalizes the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and Einstein relations to systems in rotating thermal equilibrium. By starting from the phase-space KMS relation, the authors derive new tensorial contributions and establish a novel link between spectral zero modes and transport coefficients. This provides essential microscopic constraints for modeling quantum matter under rotation, such as in the quark-gluon plasma.
main_problem: The paper derives generalized fluctuation-dissipation theorems (FDT) and Einstein relations for vector fields in a system undergoing rotating thermal equilibrium.
main_result: It establishes a model-independent generalized Einstein relation and discovers a new Einstein-type relation linking spectral zero modes to the nonrotating drag coefficient, applicable to studying rotating quantum matter.
method: The derivation starts from the exact phase-space Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) relation, generalizing it to include total angular momentum conservation, and then applying linear response theory.
model_or_system: The theory applies to general many-body quantum systems, with physical relevance highlighted in the context of the quark-gluon plasma and heavy quarkonium polarization in highly vortical media.
